nbzinbSiam

nbzinbSiam fits two regression models for overdispersed count data, with the estimation coded by hand:

Function Model Algorithm Reference implementation
nbreg() Negative binomial (NB2), log link IRLS for the coefficients, alternated with Newton-Raphson for log(theta) MASS::glm.nb()
zinbreg() Zero-inflated negative binomial EM algorithm whose M-steps are IRLS fits pscl::zeroinfl(..., dist = "negbin")

No general-purpose optimizer (optim(), nlm(), glm(), …) is used anywhere in the fitting code. Standard errors for the ZINB model come from the observed information matrix, computed with an analytic Hessian (or, optionally, numerically with numDeriv::hessian()).

This package was written for the STA 651 final project (Fall 2026, Miami University).

Installation 

# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("AshfakSiam/nbzinbSiam")

Usage 

library(nbzinbSiam)
data("bioChemists", package = "pscl")

# Negative binomial regression
fit_nb <- nbreg(art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment, data = bioChemists)
summary(fit_nb)

# Zero-inflated negative binomial regression:
# count-model covariates before |, zero-model covariates after it
fit_zinb <- zinbreg(art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment | ment,
                    data = bioChemists)
summary(fit_zinb)

# Model comparison
AIC(fit_nb, fit_zinb)

# Predictions: overall mean, count-model mean, structural-zero probability
nd <- data.frame(fem = "Women", mar = "Married", kid5 = 0, phd = 3,
                 ment = c(0, 10, 20))
predict(fit_zinb, newdata = nd, type = "response")
predict(fit_zinb, newdata = nd, type = "count")
predict(fit_zinb, newdata = nd, type = "zero")

Both fitting functions accept an offset, either as offset(log(exposure)) in the formula or through the offset argument, and a control list (nbreg_control(), zinbreg_control()) with the tolerance, the maximum number of iterations and a trace option.

Available methods

Objects of class "nbreg" and "zinbreg" support print(), summary(), coef(), vcov(), logLik() (so AIC() and BIC() work), fitted(), residuals() (response and Pearson), nobs() and predict() (with newdata). For zinbreg, predict() has type = "response" (the overall mean, (1 - pi) * mu), "count" (the count-model mean mu) and "zero" (the structural-zero probability pi).

Agreement with the reference implementations

On pscl::bioChemists, the package reproduces MASS::glm.nb() and pscl::zeroinfl(); the test suite in tests/testthat/ checks this automatically:

Quantity nbreg vs glm.nb zinbreg vs zeroinfl
Coefficients < 1e-5 < 1e-3
Standard errors < 1e-5 < 1e-3
theta (NB) / log(theta) (ZINB) < 1e-4 < 1e-3
Log-likelihood < 1e-4 < 1e-3
